reason: The text explicitly depicts non-leaders gaining agency. The dry bones—representing the ordinary people of Israel (Ezekiel 37:11)—transition from being entirely passive objects to agents with autonomous capacity: they stand upon their feet and live (וַיַּֽעַמְדוּ עַל־ רַגְלֵיהֶם, v. 10). While the passage certainly shows leaders having agency (God commanding the prophet; the prophet prophesying), its central theological message is that God restores agency to those who had lost it—the dead and hopeless. This vision fundamentally contradicts a framework where agency is exclusively concentrated among leaders.
